title: Fallen Angels starring Rose Byrne and Kelli O’Hara on Broadway #falle...
transcript: It's funny how miserably this play fails the Bechdel test, but it's also just funny. Rose Byrne and Kelli O'Hara star in the first Broadway revival of Fallen Angels by Noël Coward, which only ran for 36 performances back in 1927. They play Jane and Julia, upper-class Londoners both in affectionate but passionless marriages. With their husbands away on a golf trip and their former lover Maurice having just reported that he's going to be in London soon, it's the perfect opportunity for them to freak out and eagerly await his arrival. The delivery, the chemistry between the lead actresses, and their physical comedy is what sells this production. They really make the most out of guzzling champagne, cutting steak, or falling into the drapes, for example. While the premise is simple, the story unfolds in a sufficiently interesting, albeit predictable way — it actually feels a bit Shakespearean in how it unravels and resolves. And although the final scenes are a little drawn out and overwrought, the performances carry the energy through to the end with no problem. Rose Byrne and Kelli O'Hara are expectedly wondrous as a comedic duo, but I also loved Tracee Chimo as the eccentric housekeeper. Lighthearted yet quality comedy is difficult to achieve, but it is done well here. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: Clear recommendation with praise for the performances, chemistry, and comedy, but tempered by noting predictability and drawn-out final scenes.
